title: Functions via Graphs
summary: A graph shows a function's behavior at a glance: intercepts, increasing/decreasing intervals, maxima/minima, and symmetry (even or odd). Reading these features connects the picture to the formula.

x-intercept.plain: Where the graph crosses the x-axis.
x-intercept.in_class: Set $y=0$ and solve; a zero of the function.

y-intercept.plain: Where the graph crosses the y-axis.

concept_sections.heading: Intercepts
concept_sections.explanation: The x-intercepts are where $f(x)=0$ (the zeros); the y-intercept is $f(0)$. They anchor a sketch.

concept_sections.heading: Increasing and decreasing
concept_sections.explanation: A function increases where the graph rises left to right and decreases where it falls. Describe these as intervals of $x$.

concept_sections.heading: Maxima and minima
concept_sections.explanation: Local maxima are peaks, local minima are valleys — where the graph turns from rising to falling or vice versa.
math_steps: Peak ⇒ local max; valley ⇒ local min.

concept_sections.heading: Even and odd symmetry
concept_sections.explanation: Even functions mirror across the y-axis ($f(-x)=f(x)$); odd functions have 180° rotational symmetry about the origin ($f(-x)=-f(x)$).

concept_sections.heading: Reading a graph
concept_sections.explanation: Combine intercepts, intervals of increase/decrease, extrema, and symmetry to describe or reconstruct a function from its picture.

real_world_examples.title: A stock chart
real_world_examples.scenario: Price rises and falls over time.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Increasing/decreasing intervals and peaks/valleys describe the trend.

real_world_examples.title: A projectile's height graph
real_world_examples.scenario: Height vs time is a downward parabola.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The maximum marks the peak; the x-intercepts are launch and landing.

real_world_examples.title: A symmetric bridge arch
real_world_examples.scenario: The arch mirrors left and right.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: It models an even function, symmetric about its center line.
